items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Well a lot of the young drummers... Tony Williams... are composing and writing... I’ve always wanted to do this, it’s a salute honoring twelve great drummers... Tony Williams... are the new guys

ctx.x: Oh — a drummer knows that, yes.

Well a lot of the young drummers, well some of the older guys like Tiny Kahn was a great orchestrator, great arranger. And today, Billy Cobham, Steve Gadd, Tony Williams, a lot of these guys are composing and writing, and Harvey Mason, drummers like that you know, not only great percussion players but they’re very sensitive as to what the music is all about.
And when was it that you really felt that you could become a professional musician?

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: In Tony Williams I found he listens. He knows how to establish a groove. Definitely knows how to do that. And he had his own approach to playing cymbals and the sound of the drums.

ctx.x: You’ve got Dennis Chambers and Steve Gadd in there as well?
Right, Dennis Chambers. We’ve got Steve Gadd, Buddy Rich, Chick Webb, Big Sid Catlett, Jo Jones, Max Roach, Tony Williams.
We didn’t talk about Tony Williams yesterday. You were talking all the – a lot of drummers, but Tony Williams’s name didn’t come up. Do you want to talk about Tony now and why you included him?
